title: Android emulator: an agent sets up the SDK on its own in a KVM desktop, boots an emulator and reports the home screen
about: Covers phase 6 (opt-in hardware). The task gives no hints. The agent has to discover from desktop_start's description and the MCP instructions that it should start a desktop with kvm: true and more memory/CPUs, then install a JDK and the Android SDK into its home directory without root. deskhand ships no Android tools or template.
Verified from the manager: adb inside the desktop lists the emulator as 'device' with boot completed and the launcher in front, and a screenshot of the desktop shows the emulator window.

SLOW AND EXPENSIVE: downloads about 3 GB (JDK, SDK tools, emulator, system image), uses up to 8g / 4 CPUs and about 7 GB of disk, and takes 10–20 minutes. Run on demand only, never in CI. Needs a Docker host with /dev/kvm.

agents.prompt: Set up what you need to run an Android emulator on a deskhand desktop, boot it, and report what the emulator's home screen shows; take a screenshot. Leave the emulator running on the desktop when you are done (do not stop the desktop).

runner: Mark the agent's desktop persistent (POST /api/desktops/{id}/persistent {persistent:true}) as soon as it appears, the way a user would from the dashboard, so the checks can run after the agent's MCP session ends.
Claude Code -p exits without ending its MCP session. To run desktop_exec on the desktop afterwards, resume the agent's session id with the same token, or use docker exec -u agent.

checks.expect: the agent started a desktop with kvm and more than the default memory (it found the option on its own)
the desktop's container has /dev/kvm as a device and a memory cap above the default
inside the desktop, adb lists the emulator as 'device', boot is completed, and the launcher is the resumed activity

desktopExec.command: A=$(command -v adb || find ~ -name adb -type f -path '*platform-tools*' 2>/dev/null | head -1); $A devices; $A shell getprop sys.boot_completed; $A shell dumpsys activity activities | grep -m1 ResumedActivity

checks.expect: a screenshot of the desktop shows the Android emulator window with a booted home screen (judged by a person or a vision check)
checks.assert: manual: the emulator window shows an Android launcher

checks.expect: the final answer describes the home screen (launcher, apps, search bar or similar)
the agent saved the setup as a template that records kvm (encouraged by the instructions, not required by the task)

cleanup: DELETE /api/desktops/{id} (removes the SDK, about 7 GB, with the container)

reference_run.result: pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 11 turns, 11 min 45 s, $0.16): desktop_start(kvm, 8g, 4 cpus), Temurin JDK 17 and the command-line tools into ~/android (zip unpacked with Python because there is no unzip), sdkmanager platform-tools + emulator + android-34 google_apis x86_64, a Pixel 6 AVD, then emulator -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-audio -memory 3072 -cores 3. The first install call ran past Claude Code's 300 s MCP idle limit and was cut off; the agent polled and continued. desktop_exec now sends progress. Checked afterwards: adb 'emulator-5554 device', boot_completed 1, Android 14, NexusLauncherActivity resumed, emulator -accel-check 'KVM (version 12) is installed and usable'. No template saved. See docs/android.md.
